Winterglow is a compact, Terra Nova Nurseries selection prized for its glossy, rounded evergreen leaves, which turn a rich burgundy-red through the cold months, and its clusters of white flowers that age to soft pink, opening on sturdy red stems in early spring. Its dense, tidy habit makes it a better fit for small shade gardens and container plantings than larger species bergenias, while still providing the same tough, deer-resistant groundcover value. Divide crowded clumps every 4–5 years in spring by cutting through the woody, surface-creeping rhizomes.

Pink Dragonfly is a compact Terra Nova Nurseries bergenia bred for deep rose-pink flower clusters held on dark red stems in early spring, paired with rounded, leathery leaves that flush deep purple-red through winter cold. Its smaller stature compared to species bergenias suits it to shaded rock gardens, woodland edges, and mixed containers where a bold-textured, low-maintenance evergreen accent is wanted. It is deer- and rabbit-resistant and spreads slowly by rhizome to form a dense weed-smothering patch; divide congested clumps every 4–5 years in spring.

Bred at England's Bressingham Gardens and long a garden standard, Bressingham Ruby bears deep magenta-rose flower clusters on red stems in early spring above large, rounded, leathery leaves that turn an intense ruby-red through fall and winter, among the deepest winter color of any bergenia cultivar. Its bold, glossy foliage provides year-round structure and texture at the front of shaded borders and along shaded walkways, and it tolerates drier soil once established better than many other bergenias. Divide crowded clumps every 4–5 years in spring by cutting through the woody, surface-creeping rhizomes.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, and shear ragged summer foliage back hard after bloom to flush fresh, cleaner leaves for the rest of the season. One of the oldest and most widely grown lungwort cultivars, Mrs. Moon bears broad, bristly leaves heavily splashed with large silver spots, and clusters of funnel-shaped flowers that open pink and mature to blue-violet on the same stem in early spring, opening before most companion shade perennials leaf out. It is a magnet for early-emerging bumblebees and hummingbird migrants when little else is in bloom, and its dense, weed-suppressing foliage makes an excellent shaded groundcover. Divide congested clumps every 3–4 years in fall or right after spring bloom to maintain vigor and leaf spotting.
